preview.instructions:
You write the questions that will close the most uncertainty in the fewest asks.

You are not a question-asking machine. Every question should feel like it came
from someone who has already thought the problem through and is checking their
reasoning — not from a form.

Every question names the coverage `dimension` it serves. If it would settle one
specific open item, put that item's exact id in `about`; otherwise leave `about`
null. A question about something nobody has mentioned at all is often…

# Why we are not finished
Not yet sufficient (0 settled, 6 still open): 2 blocking open items unsettled; nothing settled yet for: purpose, users, core-behaviour, constraints, acceptance; only 0% of items are settled, against a 50% bar.
Weakest dimensions, worst first: acceptance, constraints, users, core-behaviour, purpose.

The last 1 turn(s) settled nothing new. Ask about something different, or about what is blocking a decision rather than about more detail.

## Open items you may target

questions.text: Should the tool analyze product definitions against a standard set of dimensions (like customer, problem, solution, business model, success metrics, risks), allow teams to customize which dimensions matter to them, or let teams define their own dimensions entirely?
questions.rationale: This determines the core analysis engine and what gaps the tool will actually detect—without it, nothing else in the MVP can be built.

options.label: Standard dimensions applied to all products
options.commits: Faster MVP build, predictable analysis, but may miss gaps unique to specific product types or industries.

options.label: Standard framework with team customization (skip irrelevant dimensions)
options.commits: Balances generality with flexibility; teams bypass dimensions that don't apply; more complex but still achievable in 1-2 weeks.

options.label: Teams define their own dimensions entirely
options.commits: Maximum relevance but requires teams to articulate what 'complete knowledge' means for them; harder to build smart gap detection.

questions.text: What is the primary failure mode you're trying to prevent—products that fail because they don't know their target customer, products without clear business models or success metrics, or gaps across all product dimensions equally?
questions.rationale: This clarifies what 'product knowledge gap' means and lets you scope which dimensions to emphasize when build time is limited.

options.label: Unclear or misaligned target customer (who are we building for?)
options.commits: Customer definition, audience clarity, and market validation become the MVP's primary focus; other gaps are secondary.

options.label: Missing business clarity (pricing, unit economics, go-to-market, success metrics)
options.commits: Business model, KPIs, and viability become primary; tool prevents launches without knowing what winning looks like.

options.label: General product incompleteness (gaps matter equally across all dimensions)
options.commits: Tool is a comprehensive checklist; broader scope but less deep on specific failure patterns.

questions.text: Who will actually use this tool—individual PMs or founders working alone, or cross-functional teams analyzing products together?
questions.rationale: This determines how much explanation and hand-holding the UX needs, which directly affects what you can ship in 1-2 weeks.

options.label: Individual contributors (founder or solo PM)
options.commits: Tool must be self-guided with clear reasoning; more explanation overhead in the UX; focuses on learning and discovery.

options.label: Cross-functional teams (PM, design, engineering, leadership)
options.commits: Tool surfaces gaps in a way that drives team discussion; less explanation needed; focuses on what was collectively missed.

questions.text: At what stage of the development cycle should this tool surface gaps to count as 'early enough' for teams to act—before specs are written, after specs exist but before development starts, or right before launch?
questions.rationale: This defines whether you're building pre-discovery guidance, pre-build validation, or pre-launch risk mitigation, which shapes the whole output and workflow.

options.label: Pre-specification (during research and early planning)
options.commits: Findings directly shape spec-writing; tool is part of discovery; teams haven't committed to details yet.

options.label: Pre-development (specs exist but building hasn't started)
options.commits: Tool catches incomplete specs before engineering effort; last chance to revise before dev commitment; used as pre-build checklist.

options.label: Pre-launch (product mostly built)
options.commits: Final verification before customers see it; less time to address findings but prevents obvious failures from reaching market.
